what: an .avi, .wmv or .asf output of the tools' libx264 line completed with a file that stores no presentation time for its B-frames: ffmpeg -ss 0 of a 320x240 clip decoded no picture from it, so cut --accurate and export --preset youtube said verified: false (decode step: undecodable) while audio, color, crop and 18 other tools (21 of 26 in the .avi sweep) said verified: true for the same video (tests/sweep.py with every .mp4 output swapped for .avi, .wmv and .asf: all 26 files read back with pts N/A); loudness.py's stream copy of an MP4's B-frame H.264 into .avi gave a header length of 3.093 s for 3.0 s of sound (verified: false). The #736 refusal of .mxf also said the H.264 'writes dts it rejects', when the write succeeds and stores the B-frames without their reorder (a 38-frame file decodes as 37); the same sweep found every re-encoding tool's .mpg output failing kind: ffmpeg after the encode started (MPEG-PS takes no AAC) while a dry run said completed
escaped: #488 and #736 added the container-codec table for the two muxers that refuse the tools' codecs outright; AVI and ASF take H.264 and AAC and write a file, so nothing failed, and the verifier's decode step was the only check that seeks into the file, which only cut --accurate and export run on these names. No test wrote an AVI or ASF of a re-encode or read one back after a seek; the MXF reason was written from the muxer's warning, not from a read-back
mechanism: runner._CONTAINER_ENCODERS has an .avi and a .wmv/.asf entry that refuse the H.264/HEVC encoders (and ProRes for ASF) before ffmpeg runs, dry runs included, and runner._copies_reordered_video() refuses a stream copy of B-frame video (ffprobe has_b_frames) into them from another container; an .mpg/.mpeg entry refuses the AAC encoder; the .mxf reason now says what a read-back shows. test_an_avi_or_asf_output_of_b_frame_video_is_refused_before_ffmpeg_runs measures the premise (0 frames after -ss 0 with B-frames, 50 without), refuses five tools for each extension, real and dry, and reads back the files still written
